title: Grade 7 French — Mon, Jun 16
description: L'imparfait — Day 1 of 5: Formation — stem and endings
subject: french

questions.question: How is the imperfect (l'imparfait) stem found for most verbs?
options: Take the 'nous' form of present tense and remove '-ons'
questions.explanation: The imperfect stem = the nous form of present tense minus '-ons'. E.g., parler → nous parlons → parl- (stem).

questions.question: What are the imperfect endings for je, tu, and il/elle?
questions.explanation: The imparfait endings are: je -ais, tu -ais, il/elle -ait, nous -ions, vous -iez, ils/elles -aient.

questions.question: What is the nous form of 'parler' in the present tense?
questions.explanation: Nous parlons (we speak) is the present tense nous form. Removing '-ons' gives the stem 'parl-' for the imparfait.

questions.question: Conjugate 'parler' (to speak) in l'imparfait for 'je'.
questions.explanation: Stem: parl- + ending -ais → je parlais (I was speaking / I used to speak).

questions.question: Conjugate 'finir' (to finish) in l'imparfait for 'tu'. (nous finissons → stem: finiss-)
questions.explanation: Stem of finir: finiss- (from nous finissons). tu finissais = you were finishing/used to finish.

questions.question: What ending is used for 'nous' in l'imparfait?
questions.explanation: The imparfait ending for nous is -ions. E.g., nous parlions (we were speaking).

questions.question: Conjugate 'manger' (to eat) in l'imparfait for 'il'. (nous mangeons → stem: mange-)
questions.explanation: The stem of manger is mange- (from nous mangeons, keeping the 'e' before the 'a' for pronunciation). il mangeait = he was eating.

questions.question: What is the imparfait ending for 'vous'?
questions.explanation: The imparfait ending for vous is -iez. E.g., vous parliez (you were speaking).

questions.question: Conjugate 'prendre' (to take) in l'imparfait for 'ils'. (nous prenons → stem: pren-)
questions.explanation: Stem: pren- + -aient → ils prenaient (they were taking).

questions.question: Which tense uses these endings: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient?
questions.explanation: These endings (-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient) are exclusively used for l'imparfait (the imperfect tense).

questions.question: What is the imparfait of 'aller' (to go) for 'je'? (nous allons → stem: all-)
questions.explanation: Stem: all- + -ais → j'allais (I was going / I used to go).

questions.question: Conjugate 'avoir' (to have) in imparfait for 'elle'. (nous avons → stem: av-)
questions.explanation: Stem: av- + -ait → elle avait (she was having / she had).

questions.question: Which verb has an IRREGULAR stem in l'imparfait?
questions.explanation: Être is the only verb with an irregular imparfait stem: ét- (not from nous sommes). All others follow the nous form rule.

questions.question: What is the correct imparfait form for 'nous chanter'? (chanter → nous chantons → stem: chant-)
questions.explanation: Stem: chant- + -ions → nous chantions (we were singing / we used to sing).

questions.question: Which is the correct imparfait form of 'voir' (to see) for 'tu'? (nous voyons → stem: voy-)
questions.explanation: Stem: voy- + -ais → tu voyais (you were seeing / you used to see).
